predecessors.name: Eastern Wei
predecessors.text: the 13 provinces that Hou Jing commanded south of the Yellow River

predecessors.name: Liang dynasty
predecessors.text: the capital region round Jiankang, most of Zhejiang and Shouyang

successors.name: Liang dynasty
successors.text: the capital region and Zhejiang, back to Xiao Yi's Liang after Hou Jing's fall

successors.name: Northern Qi
successors.text: Shouyang (modern central Anhui), capital of Southern Yu Province

rulers.name: Hou Jing
rulers.title: rebel general; emperor of the Han from November 551

ledger.x: 547: Hou Jing breaks with the Eastern Wei, carrying the Henan provinces he commands.
548: Hou Jing's troops collapse and he leaves Henan.
548: Hou Jing takes Shouyang by ambush.
548: Hou Jing rebels against the Liang and besieges Jiankang.
551: Hou Jing takes the throne and proclaims the Han.
552: Hou's generals north of the Yangtze go over to the Northern Qi.
552: Chen Baxian and Wang Sengbian destroy Hou Jing.
552: the Han of Hou Jing ends with his death.

wars.name: Hou Jing's rebellion
wars.outcome: Hou Jing defects from the Eastern Wei in 547, rebels against the Liang in 548, takes Jiankang in spring 549 and the Liang court dies out around him; Chen Baxian and Wang Sengbian destroy him in May 552 and his generals north of the Yangtze go to the Northern…

certainty.note: Held city by city: the extent of the capital region and of Zhejiang are readings; no frontier is fixed by any page.
